column9: stem
column14: option_a
column15: option_b
column28: explanation
column29: hint

column9: What does the word biotic mean?
column14: Living or once-living parts of an environment
column15: Nonliving physical parts of an environment
column16: Only the plants in an area
column28: Biotic means living or once-living, like plants, animals, fungi, and bacteria. A common mistake is thinking biotic means only plants; animals and microbes count too.
column29: The root bio- means life.

column9: The prefix a- means "not," so ___ factors are the nonliving parts of an environment, such as rocks, wind, and air.
column28: Abiotic means not living. Abiotic factors are the physical and chemical parts of an environment, like rocks, wind, air, temperature, and water. Don't mix it up with biotic, which means living.
column29: Add the prefix that means "not" to the word for living factors.

column9: A hiker in a northern Wisconsin forest writes down what she sees. Which item on her list is biotic?
column14: Snow on the trail
column15: A granite boulder
column28: The deer is a living organism, so it is biotic. Snow, granite, and wind are nonliving physical parts of the forest, so they are abiotic.
column29: Which item is made of cells?

column9: A class measures conditions in the Chippewa River. Which measurement is an abiotic factor?
column14: Number of brown trout
column15: Amount of algae on the rocks
column28: The speed of the current is a physical condition, so it is abiotic. Trout, algae, and mayfly larvae are all living things, so they are biotic. Don't count something as abiotic just because it lives in water.
column29: Three of these are organisms you could catch or scrape off a rock.

column9: What is the smallest unit that is considered alive?
column14: An atom
column15: A cell
column28: The cell is the smallest unit of life. Atoms and DNA molecules are not alive by themselves, and an organ is made of many cells.
column29: Every organism, even a bacterium, is made of at least one of these.

column9: An organism that is made of only one cell is called
column14: unicellular
column15: multicellular
column28: Uni- means one, so a unicellular organism is made of one cell. Multicellular organisms have many cells, and a tissue is a group of cells inside a multicellular organism.
column29: The prefix uni- means one, like a unicycle has one wheel.

column9: An organism made of many cells, like a dog or an oak tree, is called ___.
column28: Multi- means many, so an organism with many cells is multicellular. A common mistake is writing unicellular, which means one cell.
column29: The prefix you need means "many."

column9: Which molecule carries the genetic code that living things pass to their offspring?
column14: Glucose
column15: Water
column28: DNA stores the genetic code, the instructions for traits, and it is passed from parents to offspring. Glucose is a sugar for energy, and water and oxygen are not genetic material.
column29: Genes are made of this molecule.

column9: Making new organisms of the same kind is called
column14: growth
column15: reproduction
column28: Reproduction is making new organisms. Growth is getting bigger, metabolism is the chemical reactions that use energy, and homeostasis is keeping the inside of the body stable.
column29: Think about where baby animals and new plants come from.

column9: Reproduction that needs only one parent and makes offspring identical to that parent is called
column14: asexual reproduction
column15: sexual reproduction
column28: Asexual reproduction uses one parent, so the offspring get the same DNA as the parent. Sexual reproduction needs two parents and mixes their DNA.
column29: The prefix a- means "not" or "without."

column9: A female salmon lays eggs in a stream, and a male salmon releases sperm that fertilizes them. What kind of reproduction is this?
column14: Asexual reproduction
column15: Sexual reproduction
column28: Two parents combine an egg and sperm, so this is sexual reproduction. Budding is a type of asexual reproduction with only one parent.
column29: Count how many parents are involved.

column9: A strawberry plant sends out a long stem called a runner. The runner puts down roots and becomes a new strawberry plant identical to the first one. Which characteristic of life does this show?
column14: Maintaining homeostasis
column15: Changing over time as a group
column28: A new plant was made, so this is reproduction. Because there is only one parent and the new plant is identical, it is asexual reproduction. It is not evolution, which happens to a population over many generations.
column29: Something new was made. Which characteristic is about making new organisms?

column9: A change in the environment that causes an organism to react is called a
column14: stimulus
column15: response
column28: A stimulus is the signal or change, like light, heat, sound, or touch. The response is what the organism does about it. Students often swap these two words.
column29: The cause comes first; the reaction comes second. Which word is the cause?

column9: A cat smells food and runs to its bowl. The smell of the food is the stimulus, and running to the bowl is the ___.
column28: The reaction an organism makes to a stimulus is its response. Here the smell is the stimulus and running to the bowl is the response.
column29: What do we call what an organism does after it senses a stimulus?

column9: A Venus flytrap snaps shut when an insect touches the tiny hairs inside its leaf. Which characteristic of life does this show?
column14: Reproduction
column15: Responding to the environment
column17: Changing over time as a group
column28: The insect's touch is a stimulus and closing the trap is the response, so the plant is responding to its environment. Plants respond to stimuli too, not just animals.
column29: Something touched the plant, and the plant did something right away.

column9: A pill bug rolls into a tight ball when you touch it. What is the stimulus?
column14: Rolling into a ball
column15: Being touched
column16: The pill bug's hard outer shell
column28: Being touched is the stimulus that causes the reaction. Rolling into a ball is the response. The most common mistake is naming the response as the stimulus.
column29: The stimulus is what happened TO the pill bug, not what the pill bug did.

column9: After a long run you feel thirsty and drink water, which keeps the amount of water in your body steady. Keeping a stable internal environment like this is called ___.
column28: Homeostasis is keeping conditions inside the body stable, like water level, temperature, and blood sugar. Metabolism is a different idea: it is all the chemical reactions in the body.
column29: The word starts with homeo-, which means "same."

column9: In the early morning a lizard lies on a sunny rock until its body warms up. Which characteristic of life does this best show?
column14: Reproduction
column15: Maintaining homeostasis
column16: Changing over time as a group
column28: The lizard is bringing its body temperature into the range it needs, which is maintaining homeostasis. Evolution is a change in a whole population over many generations, not one lizard in one morning.
column29: What is the lizard trying to keep steady inside its body?

column9: A bald eagle catches a fish and eats it. Which characteristic of life is the eagle showing?
column14: Obtaining and using energy
column15: Reproduction
column16: Changing over time as a group
column17: Being made of only one cell
column28: Eating food is how the eagle obtains energy and materials, which its cells then use. Eagles are multicellular, and one meal has nothing to do with reproduction or evolution.
column29: Why does any animal eat?

column9: Which of these is an example of a living thing using energy?
column14: A rock warming in the sun
column15: A hummingbird beating its wings
column17: A battery sitting in a drawer
column28: The hummingbird's cells break down food to release energy that powers its wing muscles. The rock and ice are just being heated, and a battery in a drawer is not alive.
column29: Which one is an organism doing work with energy from its food?

column9: A newborn kitten weighs 100 grams. Eight weeks later it weighs 900 grams. Which characteristic of life does this show?
column14: Reproduction
column15: Responding to a stimulus
column17: Changing over time as a group
column28: The kitten is getting bigger, so it is growing and developing. Evolution is a change in a population over many generations, not one animal getting bigger.
column29: What happened to the kitten's size?

column9: What is the difference between growth and development?
column14: Growth is getting bigger; development is changing into a more mature form
column15: They mean exactly the same thing
column16: Growth happens only in plants; development happens only in animals
column17: Development is getting bigger in size; growth is changing into a new shape
column28: Growth means getting larger, often by making more cells. Development means changing form or becoming more mature, like a seedling forming flowers. Both plants and animals grow and develop.
column29: A baby gets taller (one word) and also learns to walk and matures (the other word).

column9: Which of these is an abiotic factor for a sea turtle?
column14: Seagrass it eats
column15: Ocean water temperature
column28: Water temperature is a physical condition, so it is abiotic. Seagrass, sharks, and jellyfish are all living things, so they are biotic factors.
column29: Which one is not an organism?

column9: Which of these is made of cells?
column14: A plastic bottle
column15: A blade of grass
column28: Grass is a living plant, and all living things are made of cells. Plastic, glass, and steel were never alive and have no cells.
column29: Only one of these was ever alive.

column9: Which of these is nonliving and was never part of a living thing?
column14: A maple leaf
column15: An earthworm
column28: An aluminum can is made from metal and was never part of an organism. A leaf and a feather came from living things, and an earthworm is alive.
column29: A leaf and a feather both came from organisms.

column9: Water is an abiotic factor.
column28: True. Water is not alive and is not made of cells, so it is an abiotic factor, even though living things need it.
column29: Is water made of cells?

column9: A student lists what is in a classroom fish tank. Which item is abiotic?
column14: A snail
column15: Gravel on the bottom
column28: Gravel is made of small rocks, so it is abiotic. The snail, algae, and goldfish are living, so they are biotic. Algae is tiny and looks like scum, but it is alive.
column29: Three of these are organisms, even the green film on the glass.

column9: Which is the best example of a group of organisms changing over time (evolving)?
column14: A puppy growing into an adult dog
column15: Over many generations, more rabbits in a snowy area are born with white fur
column16: A lizard regrowing its lost tail
column17: A person's skin getting a darker suntan after a whole summer of working outside in the sun
column28: Evolution is a change in a population over many generations. A puppy growing, a tail regrowing, and a tan all happen to one individual during its life, so they are not evolution.
column29: Look for the choice that involves many generations, not just one animal.

column9: Which example shows development, not just growth?
column14: A balloon getting bigger as it fills with air
column15: A caterpillar turning into a butterfly
column16: A pile of snow getting taller
column17: A puddle spreading out after a rain
column28: Development means changing into a more mature form. A caterpillar becoming a butterfly is a change in form. A balloon, snow pile, and puddle are nonliving and only change size.
column29: Which one changes its whole body form?

column9: Match each term to its meaning.
column14: Stimulus :: A signal that causes an organism to react
column15: Homeostasis :: Keeping a stable internal environment
column16: Metabolism :: All the chemical reactions in an organism
column18: Evolution :: Change in a population over many generations
column28: Stimulus: the signal. Homeostasis: keeping the inside stable. Metabolism: all the chemical reactions that build up, break down, and use energy. Reproduction: making new organisms. Evolution: a population changing over generations.
column29: Homeo- means same, and evolution is about many generations.

column9: Which organism is made of just one cell?
column14: An oak tree
column15: A paramecium
column28: A paramecium is a single-celled organism you can see under a microscope. Oak trees, houseflies, and goldfish are made of millions or more cells.
column29: Which one can you only see clearly with a microscope?

column9: What do biologists call any individual living thing?
column14: An organism
column15: A factor
column28: An organism is any individual living thing, from a bacterium to a whale. A factor is any part of an environment, and molecules and elements are not alive.
column29: The word is related to "organized."

column9: Bread mold, a pine tree, and a bluegill are all ___ factors in their environments because they are living.
column28: Living things are biotic factors. Mold is a fungus, a pine is a plant, and a bluegill is a fish, and all are alive. A common mistake is writing abiotic, which means nonliving.
column29: The root bio- means life.

column9: In a Wisconsin cornfield, which pair are BOTH abiotic factors?
column14: Corn plants and earthworms
column15: Rainfall and soil temperature
column28: Rainfall and soil temperature are both nonliving conditions. Every other pair has at least one living thing, such as corn, earthworms, crows, weeds, or insects.
column29: Rule out any pair that has even one organism in it.

column9: Which of these are biotic factors in a northern Wisconsin lake? Choose all that apply.
column14: Walleye
column15: Thickness of the ice in winter
column28: Walleye (fish), water lilies (plants), and zooplankton (tiny animals) are living, so they are biotic. Ice, sunlight, and pH are nonliving conditions, so they are abiotic.
column29: Pick only the organisms, even the tiny ones.

column9: Which of these are abiotic factors in a desert? Choose all that apply.
column14: Sand
column15: A saguaro cactus
column28: Sand, high temperature, and low rainfall are nonliving parts of the desert, so they are abiotic. The cactus, rattlesnake, and kangaroo rat are organisms, so they are biotic.
column29: Pick the things that are not made of cells.

column9: The roots of a tree grow toward a leaky water pipe underground. What is the stimulus?
column14: The roots growing
column15: Water leaking from the pipe
column28: The water from the leak is the stimulus, and the roots growing toward it is the response. Students often name the roots growing, but that is the response.
column29: What change in the environment did the roots react to?

column9: Which of these is an abiotic factor that affects how well a garden plant grows?
column14: Aphids eating its leaves
column15: Amount of sunlight it gets
column28: Sunlight is nonliving energy from the sun, so it is abiotic. Aphids, bees, and fungi are living things, so they are biotic factors that also affect the plant.
column29: Which one is not an organism?

column9: A hydra is a tiny freshwater animal. A bud grows on the side of its body, breaks off, and becomes a new hydra. This is an example of
column14: sexual reproduction
column15: asexual reproduction
column28: Budding makes a new organism from one parent, so it is asexual reproduction. There is no egg and sperm, so it is not sexual reproduction.
column29: How many parents does the new hydra have?

column9: Only animals are made of cells; plants and bacteria are not.
column28: False. ALL living things are made of cells. Plants are multicellular, and bacteria are single cells.
column29: Is a bacterium alive? What is every living thing made of?

column9: Why do living things need energy?
column14: To grow, move, repair themselves, and carry out other life processes
column15: Only to stay warm during cold weather
column17: Living things do not need energy once they have eaten and finished growing
column28: Organisms use energy for nearly everything they do: growing, moving, repairing cells, reproducing, and keeping homeostasis. Staying warm and reproducing are only two of many uses.
column29: Look for the answer that includes many life processes, not just one.

column9: Which example shows an organism maintaining homeostasis?
column14: A goose flying south in the fall because the days are getting shorter and colder
column15: After a big meal, your body brings your blood sugar back to normal
column16: A bean seed sprouting in the soil after the ground warms up in the spring
column17: A cat having a litter of kittens
column28: Bringing blood sugar back to a normal level keeps the inside of the body stable, which is homeostasis. Sprouting is growth, kittens are reproduction, and migrating is a response to the season.
column29: Look for something being brought back to a steady, normal level inside the body.

column9: Match each example to the characteristic of life it shows.
column14: A bat eating moths :: Obtains and uses energy
column15: A puppy getting taller and heavier :: Grows and develops
column16: A mimosa plant folding its leaves when touched :: Responds to the environment
column17: A rabbit giving birth to a litter :: Reproduces
column18: Your kidneys removing extra water from your blood :: Maintains homeostasis
column28: Eating gives the bat energy. Getting bigger is growth. Folding when touched is a response to a stimulus. Giving birth is reproduction. Removing extra water keeps your body's water level stable, which is homeostasis.
column29: Ask what each organism is doing: eating, getting bigger, reacting, making babies, or keeping something steady.

column9: Which list contains ONLY abiotic (nonliving) things?
column14: Rock, air, sunlight
column15: Rock, moss, air
column28: Rock, air, and sunlight are all nonliving. Each other list has a living thing hidden in it: moss, a tree, or bacteria.
column29: Check every item in each list. One living thing ruins the whole list.

column9: A patch of moss, a blue whale, and an E. coli bacterium are very different. Which characteristic do all three share?
column14: They can move from place to place
column15: They are made of cells
column17: They make their own food from sunlight
column28: All living things are made of cells, from a single-celled bacterium to a giant whale. Moss doesn't move from place to place, only the whale has bones, and the whale cannot make its own food.
column29: Pick the characteristic that is true of every living thing.

column9: A robot vacuum moves around a room, uses electricity, and turns when it bumps into a wall. Why is it NOT alive?
column14: It is made of plastic and metal parts, which are too hard to be alive
column15: It is not made of cells, has no DNA, and cannot grow or reproduce
column17: It moves in straight lines instead of choosing its own path
column28: Using energy and reacting to a bump look like characteristics of life, but the robot has no cells, no DNA, and cannot grow or make more robots. Something must show the characteristics of life, not just one or two.
column29: Think about the characteristics of life the robot is missing completely.

column9: A sand dune slowly moves across a desert and gets bigger over the years. Which observation shows it is NOT alive?
column14: It moves too slowly across the desert for anyone to see it happen
column15: It is made of sand grains, not cells, and has no DNA
column17: It gets warm during the day
column28: Getting bigger and moving do not make something alive. The dune is made of sand grains, has no cells or DNA, and cannot reproduce. Speed and location have nothing to do with being alive.
column29: Which choice names a characteristic of ALL living things that the dune lacks?

column9: A black bear hibernates all winter. Its heart rate and breathing slow way down and it does not eat for months. Is the bear alive during hibernation?
column14: No, because it is not using any energy while its heart rate and breathing are slowed
column15: Yes, because its cells are still using stored energy, just much more slowly
column16: No, because it is not responding to anything, even loud noises or bright light
column17: Yes, but only because it is warm
column28: A hibernating bear is still alive. Its cells keep using energy from stored fat, just at a much slower rate. A common mistake is thinking a slowed-down organism has stopped all life processes.
column29: Where does a hibernating bear get the energy to keep its heart beating?

column9: A gardener cuts a stem from a geranium and plants it. It grows into a new geranium with the same flower color as the first plant. Which two characteristics of life are best shown?
column14: Reproduction and passing on the same DNA
column15: Homeostasis and evolution
column16: Responding to a stimulus and homeostasis
column28: A new plant was made (reproduction), and it has the same traits because it has the same DNA as the parent. Evolution needs a population and many generations, so it does not fit.
column29: A new plant was made, and it looks the same. What carries the instructions for flower color?

column9: A student looks at an Elodea (pond plant) leaf under a microscope. Which observations show a characteristic of life? Choose all that apply.
column14: Green chloroplasts move in a circle inside each cell
column15: The leaf is made of many box-shaped cells
column18: Tiny oxygen bubbles form when the leaf is placed under a bright light
column28: Being made of cells, moving material inside the cells (which uses energy), and making oxygen in light (photosynthesis) are all characteristics of life. Color, floating, and thinness are true of nonliving things too, like green plastic.
column29: Could a piece of green plastic do it? If yes, it isn't evidence of life.

column9: Match each observation to the characteristic of life it shows.
column14: Finch beaks on an island get larger over many generations during a long drought :: Changes over time as a group
column15: A bean seed sprouts and forms its first leaves :: Grows and develops
column16: A rabbit's fur color is set by instructions it inherited from its parents :: Has a genetic code (DNA)
column17: An earthworm burrows deeper when the soil dries out :: Responds to the environment
column18: An E. coli bacterium is seen as a single cell under a microscope :: Made of cells
column28: Beaks changing over generations is evolution. Sprouting and leafing out is growth and development. Inherited instructions are the genetic code. Burrowing deeper in dry soil is a response. Seeing the cell shows the organism is made of cells.
column29: The phrase "over many generations" points to one characteristic in particular.

column9: Your body gets too hot while you exercise. Put the steps of this homeostasis response in order.
column14: Your body temperature returns to normal
column15: You exercise and your body temperature rises
column16: Sweat evaporates and cools your skin
column17: Your brain senses the rise and signals your sweat glands
column28: First the temperature rises (the change), then the brain senses it and signals the sweat glands, then sweat evaporates and cools you, and finally your temperature is back to normal. Homeostasis always starts with a change and ends back at the normal level.
column29: Something has to change before the body can sense it and react.

column9: Put the stages of a bean plant's life in order to show growth and development.
column14: A seedling forms its first green leaves
column15: The seed soaks up water and swells
column17: A root pokes out through the seed coat
column18: Flowers turn into pods with new seeds
column28: The seed swells with water, the root comes out first, then the seedling forms leaves, the adult plant flowers, and the flowers become pods with new seeds. A common mistake is putting leaves before the root.
column29: The plant needs to anchor itself and take in water before it can make leaves.

column9: A student lists everything in a backyard garden: a tomato plant, an earthworm, rainwater in a barrel, a robin, a garden hose, sunlight, a bumblebee, and a clay pot. How many items on the list are biotic?
column28: The tomato plant, earthworm, robin, and bumblebee are living, so there are 4 biotic items. Rainwater, the hose, sunlight, and the clay pot are abiotic. A common mistake is counting the rainwater because living things need it.
column29: Count only the organisms.

column9: A bean seedling is 2 cm tall on Monday. Six days later it is 14 cm tall. What was its average growth in centimeters per day?
column28: It grew 14 − 2 = 12 cm in 6 days, and 12 ÷ 6 = 2 cm per day. A common mistake is dividing 14 by 6 without first subtracting the starting height.
column29: First find how much it grew, then divide by the number of days.

column9: A student records these results. Object X: made of cells — yes; uses energy — yes; responds to touch — yes; reproduces — yes. Object Y: gets bigger — yes; made of cells — no; has DNA — no. Which conclusion is best supported?
column14: X is living and Y is nonliving
column15: Y is living and X is nonliving
column16: Both are living because both changed
column17: Both are nonliving because neither was seen growing
column28: X shows several characteristics of life, including being made of cells. Y gets bigger but has no cells and no DNA, so it is nonliving. Getting bigger alone does not prove something is alive.
column29: Which object has cells?

column9: You walk from a sunny parking lot into a dark movie theater, and your pupils get wider. Which choice correctly names the stimulus and the response?
column14: Stimulus: the darkness; Response: your pupils widen
column15: Stimulus: your pupils widen; Response: the darkness
column16: Stimulus: the movie; Response: you sit down
column17: Stimulus: your eyes; Response: the theater
column28: The change in the environment (darkness) is the stimulus, and your pupils widening to let in more light is the response. A common mistake is reversing the two.
column29: Which came first, the dark or the pupils changing?

column9: A sealed jar holds a damp cotton ball with radish seeds on it. After 3 days the seeds have sprouted and the amount of oxygen in the jar has gone down. What is the best explanation for the drop in oxygen?
column14: The sprouting seeds used oxygen to release energy from their stored food
column15: The cotton ball soaked up the oxygen as it stayed damp for 3 days
column17: The oxygen turned into water, which is why the cotton ball stayed damp for 3 days
column28: Living cells use oxygen to release energy from food (cellular respiration). Sprouting seeds need lots of energy to grow, so the oxygen drops. This is evidence that the seeds are alive and using energy.
column29: Growing takes energy. What do cells use oxygen for?

column9: Which statement correctly compares unicellular and multicellular organisms?
column14: Unicellular organisms do every life process in one cell; multicellular organisms have specialized cells
column15: Unicellular organisms are not truly alive, because one cell is too small to carry out every life process
column16: Multicellular organisms do not need energy
column28: A single cell, like a paramecium, must do everything to stay alive. In a multicellular organism, like you, different cells do different jobs, such as muscle cells and nerve cells. Both kinds are alive, use energy, and have DNA.
column29: Think about how one cell could do every job versus how your body splits up jobs.

column9: A trout stream in Wisconsin warms up after the trees along its banks are cut down. Which statement correctly describes what happened?
column14: Trees (biotic) were cut, raising the water temperature (abiotic), which can harm the trout (biotic)
column15: Water temperature is a biotic factor, because the trout and other living things in the stream depend on it
column16: Trees are abiotic because they do not move
column17: Trout are abiotic because they live underwater
column28: Trees are living (biotic). Without their shade, more sun hits the water and raises its temperature, an abiotic factor. Trout need cold water, so this abiotic change affects a biotic factor. Biotic and abiotic factors affect each other.
column29: Label each thing as living or nonliving first, then follow the chain.

column9: A plastic plant and a real plant sit side by side in a sunny window for a month. Which observation shows that only the real plant is alive?
column14: Both plants stay green the whole month in the window
column15: Only one plant grows new leaves during the month
column28: Growing new leaves is growth and development, which only a living thing can do. Being green, casting shadows, and sitting in a pot are true of both, so they do not tell them apart.
column29: Look for something that one plant does and the other cannot.

column9: An amoeba moves toward a piece of food and wraps itself around it. Which TWO characteristics of life are shown?
column14: Responding to the environment and obtaining energy
column15: Evolution and reproduction
column16: Homeostasis and evolution, because the amoeba changes its shape
column28: The amoeba senses the food and moves toward it (a response), then takes it in to get energy and materials. Nothing new is made, so it is not reproduction, and one amoeba cannot evolve.
column29: What did the amoeba sense, and why does it want the food?

column9: When a population of organisms changes over many generations, biologists say the population has ___.
column28: A population that changes over many generations has evolved. Evolution happens to groups over time, not to one individual during its life.
column29: This characteristic of life is about change in a group over a long time.

column9: A goldfish lives in fresh water. Water keeps soaking into its body, and its kidneys pump the extra water back out so its body stays balanced. Which characteristic of life is this?
column14: Maintaining homeostasis
column15: Changing over time as a group
column28: The kidneys keep the water level inside the fish stable, which is homeostasis. Evolution would need a whole population over many generations.
column29: What is being kept steady inside the fish?

column9: Which reasons show that wind is nonliving? Choose all that apply.
column14: It is not made of cells
column15: It has no DNA
column16: It moves from place to place
column28: Wind has no cells, no DNA, and cannot reproduce, so it lacks key characteristics of life. Moving and being strong don't prove anything either way, because many living and nonliving things move.
column29: Choose the reasons that name a characteristic of life that wind is missing.

column9: Which observations show a pet hamster maintaining homeostasis? Choose all that apply.
column14: It drinks more water on a hot day
column15: It fluffs up its fur when the room gets cold
column16: It has a litter of babies
column17: It eats seeds and grows larger
column18: It runs on its wheel at night
column28: Drinking more water keeps its water level steady, and fluffing its fur traps heat to keep its body temperature steady. Having babies is reproduction, and eating and growing is energy use and growth.
column29: Which actions keep something inside the hamster's body steady?

column9: Which pair correctly matches an organism with how it obtains energy?
column14: Grass: makes its own food using sunlight
column15: Deer: makes its own food from sunlight
column17: Wolf: absorbs sunlight through its fur
column28: Grass is a plant that makes its own food by photosynthesis. Deer and wolves must eat other organisms, and oak trees do not eat insects.
column29: Which organisms can make their own food?

column9: The process plants and algae use to make sugar from carbon dioxide and water using light energy is called ___.
column28: Photosynthesis uses light energy to make sugar, which is how plants and algae obtain energy. A common mistake is writing respiration, which breaks sugar down to release its energy.
column29: Photo- means light.

column9: A student tests three samples. Sample A has cells and uses sugar. Sample B has no cells and gets bigger in water. Sample C has cells, but no activity is seen today. Which samples could be living?
column14: A only
column15: A and C
column28: A shows cells and energy use. C has cells and could be dormant, like a seed or a hibernating animal, so it could still be living. B has no cells, so it cannot be living even though it gets bigger.
column29: Something can be alive even when it seems inactive. What do A and C have in common?

column9: Algae in a lake need sunlight to make food. After a big storm, the lake water becomes very muddy. What will most likely happen to the algae?
column14: Less light reaches them, so they make less food and their population drops
column15: They grow faster because the mud carries extra food for the algae to eat
column16: Nothing changes, because mud is abiotic and abiotic factors can't affect living things
column28: Mud blocks sunlight, an abiotic factor the algae need for photosynthesis, so they make less food and their numbers drop. Abiotic factors do affect living things, even though they are not alive.
column29: What does muddy water block?

column9: Which of these are alive? Choose all that apply.
column14: Moss on a tree trunk
column15: A cloud
column16: A sea sponge growing on a reef
column28: Moss is a plant, a sea sponge is an animal, and bread mold is a fungus, so all three are alive. Clouds, quartz, and robots are not made of cells. Many students miss the sponge because it doesn't move.
column29: A living thing doesn't have to move. Which ones are made of cells?

column9: Under a microscope, a student compares a thin layer of onion skin with a piece of clear plastic wrap. Both look thin and clear to the eye. Which observation shows which one came from a living thing?
column14: The onion skin is made of many cells, each with a nucleus
column15: The plastic wrap is shinier
column17: The plastic wrap is easier to focus on because it is so thin
column28: Only things that are or were living are made of cells, and onion cells each have a nucleus holding DNA. Shine, smell, and how easy it is to focus are not characteristics of life.
column29: Which choice names a characteristic of life?

column9: A monarch butterfly lays eggs on milkweed, its caterpillar eats milkweed leaves, it turns into a butterfly, and it flies south when the days get shorter. Which part of the monarch's life best shows responding to the environment?
column14: Flying south when the days get shorter
column15: Laying eggs on milkweed
column17: Changing from a caterpillar into a butterfly
column28: Shorter days are a stimulus, and flying south is the response. Laying eggs is reproduction, eating is obtaining energy, and changing form is development.
column29: Find the part where a change in the environment triggers an action.

column9: A Wisconsin farmer spreads lime (a crushed rock powder) on a field to raise the soil pH, then plants alfalfa. Over the summer, earthworms increase and more birds visit. Which of these are abiotic factors in this story? Choose all that apply.
column14: Soil pH
column15: Alfalfa
column28: Soil pH, lime, and sunlight are nonliving, so they are abiotic. Alfalfa, earthworms, and birds are organisms, so they are biotic. Notice how the abiotic change (pH) affected the biotic factors.
column29: Pick everything in the list that is not an organism.

column9: A houseplant is left in a dark closet for a week. Its stem grows long and pale and bends toward a crack of light under the door. Which characteristics of life are shown?
column14: Growth and responding to the environment
column15: Reproduction and evolution
column17: None, because the plant was in the dark and could not make food
column28: The stem got longer (growth), and it bent toward the light (a response to a stimulus). One plant in one week cannot evolve, and no new plant was made.
column29: Two things happened to the stem: it changed length and it changed direction.

column9: Scientists put a jellyfish gene for a glowing protein into a bacterium. The bacterium then made the glowing protein. What does this best show?
column14: All living things share the same genetic code, so one species' cells can read another's DNA
column15: Bacteria can evolve into jellyfish
column16: The bacterium was maintaining homeostasis by making a new protein to keep its insides stable
column28: The bacterium could read the jellyfish's gene and build the protein because all organisms use the same basic genetic code in DNA. This is not evolution (that takes many generations in a population), and jellyfish are not made of bacteria.
column29: Why could a bacterium follow instructions written for a jellyfish?

column9: A home thermostat turns the furnace on when the house cools below 68 °F and turns it off when the house warms back up. Which statement is best?
column14: It works like homeostasis by keeping conditions stable, but the house is not alive because it is not made of cells, has no DNA, and cannot reproduce
column15: The house is alive because it keeps a stable internal environment
column16: The thermostat is biotic because it responds to temperature
column17: This is evolution because the temperature changes over time
column28: Keeping a steady temperature is LIKE homeostasis, but one look-alike feature does not make something alive. The house and thermostat lack cells, DNA, growth, and reproduction. Evolution is a population changing over generations, not a daily temperature swing.
column29: Can a nonliving thing copy one characteristic of life without being alive?

column9: Tardigrades ("water bears") are tiny animals that can dry out and stop almost all activity for years, then become active again when water returns. While dried out, how are they best described?
column14: Nonliving, because they are not moving, eating, or doing anything at all while they are dried out
column15: Living but dormant, because their cells and DNA are intact and they can become active again
column17: Dead, and then brought back to life by the water
column28: A dried-out tardigrade is dormant: its cells and DNA are still intact and it can resume all its life processes. Not moving does not mean not living, and dead organisms cannot come back to life.
column29: Could something that was truly dead become active again just by adding water?

column9: A cloud forms, grows bigger, drifts across the sky, and splits into smaller clouds. Which characteristics of life does a cloud SEEM to show, even though it is not alive? Choose all that apply.
column14: Growth
column15: Being made of cells
column28: The cloud gets bigger (looks like growth) and splits into new clouds (looks like reproduction). It has no cells or DNA, and nothing in the description shows it keeping its inside stable. A few look-alike features are not enough to make something alive.
column29: Only pick what the description actually says the cloud does.

column9: A student claims, "Moving from place to place is a characteristic of all living things." Which example best shows the claim is wrong?
column14: An oak tree is alive, but it does not move from place to place
column15: A river moves, but it is not alive
column17: A robot vacuum moves from room to room on its own, but it is not alive
column28: To disprove "all living things move," you need a living thing that doesn't move from place to place, like an oak tree. The river and robot show that moving things can be nonliving, which is a different claim.
column29: The claim is about ALL living things. What kind of example would break it?

column9: A single bacterium divides into two every 20 minutes, and every new cell keeps dividing at the same rate. Starting with 1 bacterium, how many bacteria will there be after 2 hours?
column28: 2 hours = 120 minutes = 6 periods of 20 minutes. The number doubles each time: 1 → 2 → 4 → 8 → 16 → 32 → 64. A common mistake is multiplying 6 × 2 = 12 instead of doubling six times.
column29: Count the 20-minute periods, then double the number once for each period.

column9: A student wants to test whether dry brine shrimp eggs from a pet store are alive. Which plan would give the best evidence?
column14: Put the eggs in warm salt water and check daily for hatching, growth, and movement
column15: Weigh the eggs on a scale
column16: Look closely at the eggs' color with a hand lens to see if they look bright and healthy
column17: Shake the container and listen to them
column28: Giving the eggs the conditions they need and watching for hatching and growth tests characteristics of life directly. Mass, color, and sound are true of nonliving things too, so they can't show life.
column29: Which plan gives the eggs a chance to show a characteristic of life?

column9: A space probe collects an unknown sample. Which observations would support the idea that the sample is a living organism? Choose all that apply.
column14: Under a microscope it is made of cells
column15: It contains DNA or similar genetic material
column16: It is shaped like a sphere
column17: Over several days the number of units increases as each one divides
column19: It takes in nutrients and gives off waste gases
column28: Cells, genetic material, reproduction (dividing), and using materials for energy (taking in nutrients, giving off waste) are characteristics of life. Shape and reflecting light are true of rocks and ice too.
column29: Cross out any observation that a rock could also have.

column9: Rust slowly spreads across a bike chain, and fuzzy mold slowly spreads across a slice of bread. What is the key difference between them?
column14: The mold is made of cells and reproduces; the rust is a chemical reaction with no cells
column15: The rust is alive but the mold is not
column16: Both are alive because both spread
column17: Both are abiotic, because both of them grow on nonliving objects instead of in soil or water
column28: Mold is a fungus: it is made of cells, uses the bread for energy, and reproduces. Rust is iron reacting with oxygen and water; it spreads but has no cells or DNA. Spreading alone does not mean something is alive.
column29: Which one would you see as cells under a microscope?

column9: Each nonliving thing below does something that looks like a characteristic of life. Match each one to the characteristic it resembles.
column14: A snowball rolling downhill and getting bigger :: Growth
column15: An automatic door opening when you walk up to it :: Responding to a stimulus
column16: A gas engine taking in fuel and releasing energy :: Using energy
column17: A computer virus making copies of itself on other computers :: Reproduction
column28: The snowball gets bigger (looks like growth). The door reacts to you (looks like a response). The engine takes in fuel and releases energy (like metabolism). The computer virus copies itself (looks like reproduction). None of them is made of cells or has DNA.
column29: Ask what each object does that a living thing also does.

column9: For many years, people fished a lake heavily and kept the biggest yellow perch. Now the lake's perch population has more fish that become adults at a smaller size. Which characteristic of life does this best show?
column14: Changing over time as a group (evolving)
column15: Growing and developing, since the adults are now smaller
column28: The traits of the whole population shifted over many generations, which is evolution. Growth is tempting because the question is about size, but no single fish changed; the population changed.
column29: Is this about one fish during its life, or the whole population over many years?

column9: When an amoeba divides in two, it is reproduction. When a skin cell on your arm divides in two, it is NOT reproduction. Why?
column14: The amoeba is a whole organism, so dividing makes a new organism; your skin cell is only part of you, so its division helps you grow and repair
column15: Skin cells have no DNA
column17: Skin cells only divide during homeostasis
column28: In a unicellular organism, one cell IS the organism, so cell division makes a new organism. In a multicellular organism, cell division makes more cells for the same organism, which is growth and repair. Both cells have DNA.
column29: Does dividing the skin cell make a new person?

column9: Two sealed jars each hold a thermometer. Jar A has sprouting pea seeds. Jar B has the same number of pea seeds that were boiled first. After 24 hours, Jar A is 2 °C warmer than Jar B. What is the best conclusion?
column14: The sprouting seeds are alive and give off heat as they use energy; boiling killed Jar B's seeds
column15: Boiled seeds are more alive than sprouting seeds
column16: Nothing happened, because the jars are abiotic
column17: Jar A warmed up because sprouting seeds are heavier, and heavier seeds hold more heat from the room
column28: Living cells release heat when they break down food for energy. The boiled seeds are dead, so they release no heat; they act as the control. Mass does not produce heat.
column29: What do living cells give off when they use energy? Which jar is the control?

column9: A student claims, "Anything that responds to a stimulus must be alive." Which example best shows the claim is wrong?
column14: A smartphone screen lights up when you touch it
column15: A plant bends toward a window
column16: A dog barks at a loud noise
column17: A worm wriggles away from a bright flashlight beam
column28: The phone responds to touch but is not made of cells, has no DNA, and cannot reproduce, so responding alone does not prove life. The plant, dog, and worm are living things, so they support the claim instead of breaking it.
column29: To disprove the claim, you need something that responds but is NOT alive.

column9: Which characteristics of life does a single bacterium share with a blue whale? Choose all that apply.
column14: Made of cells
column15: Uses DNA as its genetic code
column28: Both are made of cells, use DNA, use energy, and maintain homeostasis, because these are true of all living things. A bacterium is unicellular, and bacteria reproduce asexually, while whales reproduce sexually.
column29: Pick only what is true of EVERY living thing.

column9: Scientists find a woolly mammoth frozen in ice. It still has cells and some DNA, but it has been dead for thousands of years. How should it be classified?
column14: Biotic, because it was once living, but it is not a living organism now
column15: A living organism, because it still has some of its DNA after thousands of years
column17: A living organism, because it is made of cells
column28: Once-living things and their remains count as biotic, but the mammoth is not alive now because its cells no longer use energy, grow, or respond. Having cells and DNA is not enough; a living thing must carry out life processes.
column29: Is anything inside the mammoth still using energy or growing?

column9: A field guide says: "Ferns are multicellular, make their own food from sunlight, stay rooted in one place, and reproduce with spores." Which choice lists characteristics of life that this description does NOT give direct evidence of?
column14: Maintaining homeostasis and evolving
column15: Being made of cells and obtaining energy
column17: Reproducing and being made of cells
column28: Multicellular means made of cells, making food from sunlight is obtaining energy, and spores are reproduction. Nothing in the description mentions keeping conditions stable or a population changing over generations. (It also skips a few others, but every other choice names something the description does show.)
column29: Match each phrase in the description to a characteristic, then see what is left over.

column9: Coral reefs can look like rocks. Which evidence best supports the idea that coral is alive?
column14: Coral is made of tiny animals called polyps that catch food and reproduce
column15: Coral is hard
column16: Coral is found in the ocean
column17: Coral comes in bright colors, just like many of the fish that swim around the reef
column28: Coral is a colony of animals (polyps) that are made of cells, eat, and reproduce. Being hard, living in the ocean, or being colorful are true of rocks and shells too, so they don't show life.
column29: Which choice names characteristics of life?

column9: A student says, "My houseplant isn't alive because it doesn't move around, eat, or make noise." Which facts show the plant IS alive? Choose all that apply.
column14: It is made of cells
column15: It makes its own food by photosynthesis
column19: It bends toward the window over several days
column28: Cells, making food (obtaining energy), growing, and bending toward light (responding) are characteristics of life. Being green or sitting in a pot is true of a plastic plant too. Plants obtain energy without eating.
column29: Would a fake plastic plant also have this property? If so, leave it out.

column9: Scientists raised fruit flies in very dry air for 30 generations. The final population loses water much more slowly than the starting population did. But a single fly moved from moist air to dry air does not change how fast it loses water. What does this show?
column14: Populations can evolve over generations, but a single individual does not evolve
column15: Each fly evolved during its own life
column16: The flies were only maintaining homeostasis by keeping their water levels steady
column17: Dry air is a biotic factor
column28: The change showed up in the population across many generations, not in one fly during its life. That is the difference between evolution (a group over time) and an individual's response. Dry air is abiotic.
column29: Compare what happened to the population with what happened to one fly.

column9: In some Wisconsin lakes, thick ice and snow cover the surface all winter, and many fish die by late winter. Which chain of events best explains this?
column14: Snow blocks sunlight, so algae and plants make less oxygen, and the fish run out of dissolved oxygen
column15: The ice is a biotic factor, so it uses up the oxygen and competes with the fish under the frozen surface
column17: The fish evolve to leave the lake
column28: Without light, plants and algae can't do photosynthesis, so less oxygen enters the water. Low oxygen, an abiotic factor, can kill fish, which are biotic. Ice is abiotic, and fish don't evolve in one winter.
column29: Follow the sunlight: what do plants and algae make with it?

column9: Which pair of examples shows the SAME characteristic of life?
column14: A bear eating salmon and a maple tree making sugar in its leaves
column15: A bird building a nest and a seed sprouting
column16: A cat having kittens and a snake shedding its skin as it grows
column17: A child growing taller and a lizard warming itself on a sunny rock
column28: Eating salmon and making sugar by photosynthesis are both ways of obtaining energy. In the other pairs the two examples show different characteristics: getting ready to reproduce vs. growth, reproduction vs. growth, and growth vs. homeostasis.
column29: Name the characteristic for each example in a pair, then see which pair matches.

column9: A student says, "Abiotic factors don't really matter to organisms, because abiotic factors aren't alive." Which example best shows the student is wrong?
column14: Corn plants in a field wilt and stop growing during a drought
column15: A deer eats grass
column17: A fox hunts and eats a rabbit to get the energy it needs to raise its young
column28: A drought is a lack of water, an abiotic factor, and it directly harms the corn. The other examples show living things affecting other living things, which doesn't address the claim about abiotic factors.
column29: You need an example where something nonliving affects a living thing.

column9: A student compares a real goldfish with a battery-powered robot fish that swims around a tank. Which characteristics does ONLY the real goldfish have? Choose all that apply.
column14: Made of cells
column15: Moves through the water
column28: Only the real fish is made of cells, has DNA, can reproduce, and grows. Both of them move, and both use energy (food for the fish, a battery for the robot), so those don't tell them apart.
column29: Cross out anything the robot can also do.

column9: Lichen grows in crusty patches on a rock. Lichen is made of a fungus and an alga living together. A student says the lichen is abiotic because it is crusty and stuck to a rock. Which statement is best?
column14: The lichen is biotic because it is made of living fungus and alga cells; the rock is abiotic
column15: Both the lichen and the rock are biotic, since the living lichen is growing right on the rock
column16: Both the lichen and the rock are abiotic
column17: The lichen becomes abiotic in winter
column28: Lichen is made of living cells from a fungus and an alga, so it is biotic. The rock is nonliving, so it is abiotic. Looking crusty or sitting on a rock doesn't change whether something is made of living cells.
column29: What is lichen made of?
